Prepare censored observations for the additive weight model

Source: R/censoring.R
prepare_censoring.Rd

Turns the censoring labels produced by curveRcore (classify_censoring_multiplate(): censor_type, censor_lower, censor_upper) into the columns the additive model's censored likelihood needs.

Usage

prepare_censoring(
  df,
  censor_col = "censor_type",
  lower_col = "censor_lower",
  upper_col = "censor_upper",
  yi_col = "yi",
  se_col = "cv_i",
  se_bound_col = NULL,
  curve_col = "curve_id"
)

Arguments

df

Data frame containing yi (log10 response) and se_col.

censor_col

Column holding "none", "left", "interval", "right" (or NA). NULL means no censoring: every row is treated as quantified.

lower_col, upper_col

Natural-scale censoring bounds.

yi_col

Name of the log10 response column.

se_col

Name of the measurement SE column (log10 scale).

se_bound_col

Optional column with the measurement SE at the censoring limit. NULL (default) uses the nearest quantified sample of the same curve.

curve_col

Column identifying the curve (used to find the nearest quantified sample). Ignored if absent.

Value

df with added columns:

cens_flag

brms censoring code: 0 quantified, -1 left, 1 right, 2 interval. NA if the row is censored but its bound is missing (such rows cannot be used).

yi

Overwritten for censored rows by the (log10) censoring limit: the upper bound for left, the lower bound for right and interval.

yi2

Upper bound for interval rows, otherwise equal to yi.

se_meas

Measurement SE used by the model: the row's own SE for quantified rows, the SE at the limit for censored rows.

bound

log10 censoring limit (NA for quantified rows).

In plain terms

A sample outside the quantifiable range of the standard curve is not a noisy number; it is a sample we only know to be below (or above) some limit. Treating its extrapolated back-calculated value as an ordinary measurement is wrong, and so is giving it a weight. Instead the model uses the statement "the true value is below the lower limit" (left-censored), "above the upper limit" (right-censored) or "between the two" (interval). This function builds, for every row, the censoring flag and the limit that statement refers to.

For a censored row the model also needs to know how precisely the limit itself is determined. That is the measurement SD at the limit, not the (extrapolated, usually huge) SE of the row's own back-calculated value. By default it is taken from the quantified sample of the same curve whose value is closest to the limit; supply se_bound_col to use a better source (for example the SE read off the curve's precision grid at the limit).

Scales

censor_lower/censor_upper are on the natural concentration scale and must be on the same scale as the response yi (see the dilution_col argument of fit_additive_weight()). They are converted to log10 here.

See also

fit_additive_weight()

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  curve_id = "c1",
  yi = c(0.1, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6, NA),
  cv_i = c(NA, 0.12, 0.08, 0.15, NA),
  censor_type = c("left", "none", "none", "none", "right"),
  censor_lower = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 70),
  censor_upper = c(5, NA, NA, NA, NA))
prepare_censoring(d, se_col = "cv_i")
#>   curve_id       yi cv_i censor_type censor_lower censor_upper      yi2
#> 1       c1 0.698970   NA        left           NA            5 0.698970
#> 2       c1 0.800000 0.12        none           NA           NA 0.800000
#> 3       c1 1.200000 0.08        none           NA           NA 1.200000
#> 4       c1 1.600000 0.15        none           NA           NA 1.600000
#> 5       c1 1.845098   NA       right           70           NA 1.845098
#>   cens_flag se_meas    bound
#> 1        -1    0.12 0.698970
#> 2         0    0.12       NA
#> 3         0    0.08       NA
#> 4         0    0.15       NA
#> 5         1    0.15 1.845098
